title: 第五課：牛肉麵真好吃
zh1:
月美：很多人都說臺灣有不少有名的小吃。
明華：是啊！牛肉麵、小籠包、臭豆腐……都很好吃。
月美：你最喜歡吃什麼？
明華：牛肉麵。牛肉好吃，湯也好喝。
月美：這麼好吃，我很想吃。
明華：我知道一家有名的牛肉麵店，我們一起去吃，怎麼樣？
月美：太好了！
明華：我們明天去。一定要點大碗的。
py1:
Yuèměi：Hěnduō rén dōu shuō Táiwān yǒu bùshǎo yǒumíng de xiǎochī.
Mínghuá：Shì a! Niúròumiàn, xiǎolóngbāo, chòudòufǔ... dōu hěn hǎochī.
Yuèměi：Nǐ zuì xǐhuān chī shénme?
Mínghuá：Niúròumiàn. Niúròu hǎochī, tāng yě hǎohē.
Yuèměi：Zhème hǎochī, wǒ hěn xiǎng chī.
Mínghuá：Wǒ zhīdào yì jiā yǒumíng de niúròumiàn diàn, wǒmen yìqǐ qù chī, zěnmeyàng?
Yuèměi：Tài hǎo le!
Mínghuá：Wǒmen míngtiān qù. Yídìng yào diǎn dà wǎn de.
en1:
Yuemei：Many people say Taiwan has quite a few famous snacks.
Minghua：That’s right! Beef noodles, xiaolongbao, and stinky tofu are all delicious.
Yuemei：What do you like to eat most?
Minghua：Beef noodles. The beef tastes good, and the soup is delicious too.
Yuemei：It sounds so delicious. I really want to try it.
Minghua：I know a famous beef noodle shop. How about going there together?
Yuemei：Great!
Minghua：Let’s go tomorrow. You definitely have to order a large bowl.
zh2:
月美：昨天晚上那家餐廳的菜很好吃，可是有一點辣。
安同：我也怕辣，所以我喜歡自己做飯。
月美：你做飯做得怎麼樣？
安同：我做得不好。妳會做飯嗎？
月美：會。我的甜點也做得不錯。
安同：我最喜歡吃甜點。妳可以教我嗎？
月美：好的，這個週末，你到我家來。
安同：好啊！謝謝妳。
py2:
Yuèměi：Zuótiān wǎnshàng nà jiā cāntīng de cài hěn hǎochī, kěshì yǒu yìdiǎn là.
Āntóng：Wǒ yě pà là, suǒyǐ wǒ xǐhuān zìjǐ zuòfàn.
Yuèměi：Nǐ zuòfàn zuò de zěnmeyàng?
Āntóng：Wǒ zuò de bù hǎo. Nǐ huì zuòfàn ma?
Yuèměi：Huì. Wǒ de tiándiǎn yě zuò de búcuò.
Āntóng：Wǒ zuì xǐhuān chī tiándiǎn. Nǐ kěyǐ jiāo wǒ ma?
Yuèměi：Hǎode, zhè ge zhōumò, nǐ dào wǒ jiā lái.
Āntóng：Hǎo a! Xièxie nǐ.
en2:
Yuemei：The food at that restaurant last night was delicious, but it was a little spicy.
Antong：I can’t take spicy food either, so I like to cook for myself.
Yuemei：How well do you cook?
Antong：I don’t cook well. Can you cook?
Yuemei：Yes. I make desserts pretty well too.
Antong：I like desserts most. Could you teach me?
Yuemei：Sure. Come to my place this weekend.
Antong：Great! Thank you.

act:
I. Street Vendor Food Is Good
【目標 Goal】Learn to recognize and name common Taiwanese snacks.
【做法 Task】Compete with classmates to name as many Taiwanese street foods as possible. Show food pictures and say their Chinese names.
【例】臭豆腐、小籠包、牛肉麵、蔥油餅、車輪餅、煎餃……

II. Tell Us What You Think
【目標 Goal】Use 很, 太, or 有一點 to evaluate familiar objects and prices.
【做法 Task】Listen to each price and give an appropriate evaluation.
【例】A：一碗牛肉麵一百八十塊錢。
B：有一點貴。

A：一杯咖啡十五塊。
B：太便宜了！

III. Talent Contest
【目標 Goal】Describe what someone can do and how well they can do it.
【做法 Task】Ask classmates about their skills and proficiency, then record the answers. Suggested skills: making desserts, swimming, taking photos, basketball, soccer, making xiaolongbao, and tennis.
【例】你會不會做飯？
會，我會做飯，可是做得不好。／不會，我不會做飯。

IV. Asking for Help
【目標 Goal】Learn to ask someone for help with learning a skill.
【做法 Task】Choose a skill that a classmate does well and ask that classmate to teach you.
【例】我想學做小籠包，你可以教我嗎？
cult:
街頭小吃的排隊現象 Queuing up at Food Stands
在臺灣，街頭路邊攤或小吃店前大排長龍是常見的日常景象。這些攤位通常在固定的時間與地點營業。只要食物新鮮、便宜又美味，不論天氣多麼惡劣，攤位前往往都會排起長長的人龍。只需花少許零錢，人們就能買到包子、蔥油餅、車輪餅（紅豆餅）或煎餃等美味小吃。

臺灣的路邊攤文化 Street Vendors in Taiwan
路邊攤在臺灣極為常見，源自早期農業社會的農民集市和廟會慶典。如今，在景區、住宅區、市場邊緣、商業區周邊、騎樓下、街道上，甚至考場外與廟會期間，都能看到各式路邊攤。商品從日用品、美食小吃到伴手禮應有盡有。路邊攤移動性高，有時會影響交通、社區安寧或市容；若能適度規劃與規範，也能為城市增添活力與特色。

blocks.label: 功能
blocks.text: 有一點 + state verb expresses a mildly negative evaluation or dissatisfaction from the speaker.
blocks.ex:
這碗牛肉麵有一點辣。
This bowl of beef noodles is a little spicy.
那支手機有一點貴。
That cell phone is a little expensive.
他的房子有一點舊。
His house is a little old.

blocks.label: Usage Restrictions
blocks.text: Because the pattern already implies a negative evaluation, it has no negative form. It cannot normally modify a positive state verb used as praise; for example, 他妹妹有一點漂亮 is unacceptable.

blocks.label: 功能
blocks.text: 得 follows a verb and introduces a complement describing the result, state, or degree of an action.
blocks.ex:
他學中文學得不錯。
He learns Chinese quite well.
王伯母做越南菜做得很好。
Auntie Wang cooks Vietnamese food very well.
這種手機賣得很好。
This type of phone sells well.

blocks.label: 結構
blocks.text: With a transitive verb and object, either repeat the verb (V + O + V + 得 + complement) or move the object to topic position (O, S + V + 得 + complement).
blocks.ex:
你做飯做得真好吃。
You cook really well.
中文，你說得很好。
You speak Chinese very well.
這種甜點，他做得很好吃。
He makes this kind of dessert very well.

blocks.label: 否定
blocks.text: Place 不 before the complement, not before the verb.
blocks.ex:
他做甜點做得不好。
He does not make desserts well.
他的咖啡賣得不好。
His coffee does not sell well.

blocks.label: 疑問
blocks.text: Use 怎麼樣, A-not-A, or 嗎 in the complement to form questions.
blocks.ex:
他做飯做得怎麼樣？
How well does he cook?
中文，他說得好不好？
Does he speak Chinese well?
他打籃球打得好嗎？
Does he play basketball well?

blocks.label: 功能
blocks.text: The auxiliary verb 會 expresses a skill acquired through learning or practice.
blocks.ex:
陳小姐會做飯。
Miss Chen can cook.
他們兄弟姐妹都會游泳。
All the siblings know how to swim.
他哥哥會踢足球。
His older brother knows how to play soccer.

blocks.label: 否定
blocks.text: The negative form of 會 is 不會.
blocks.ex:
他的媽媽不會做飯。
His mother cannot cook.
我的家人都不會打棒球。
No one in my family knows how to play baseball.

blocks.label: 疑問
blocks.text: Use 會…嗎 or 會不會 to ask whether someone has learned a skill.
blocks.ex:
你會做甜點嗎？
Do you know how to make desserts?
你會不會說中文？
Can you speak Chinese?
你的姐姐會不會做飯？
Can your older sister cook?

blocks.label: 功能
blocks.text: The preposition 到 marks the destination toward which an action is directed. It is normally used with a main verb such as 來 or 去.
blocks.ex:
他這個週末到臺灣來。
He is coming to Taiwan this weekend.
老師明天到臺北來。
The teacher is coming to Taipei tomorrow.
明天我們可以到那家店去。
We can go to that shop tomorrow.

blocks.label: 否定
blocks.text: Place 不 before 到, not before the main verb.
blocks.ex:
王先生明天不到臺北來。
Mr. Wang is not coming to Taipei tomorrow.
他們不到那家餐廳去。
They are not going to that restaurant.

blocks.label: 疑問
blocks.text: Use 到不到 in an A-not-A question.
blocks.ex:
你妹妹到不到臺灣來？
Is your younger sister coming to Taiwan?
他們到不到我家來？
Are they coming to my house?

blocks.label: Colloquial Usage
blocks.text: In Taiwan and southern China, 到 is also commonly used directly as a verb meaning to come or go.
blocks.ex:
我們要到哪一家？
Which one should we go to?
他們明天晚上要到王老師家。
They are going to Teacher Wang’s home tomorrow evening.
歡迎你到我家。
Welcome to my home.
